final_rationale: No new admissible evidence was provided. The change is based on the Actor narrowing the claim from an unsupported clean certification position to a policy-bounded, caveated position that better matches the existing record. Admissible evidence does support limited statements that aggregate launch readiness is above threshold and that rehearsal had no severity-one incidents, and public risk-management guidance supports monitored deployment. But the same record still shows an unresolved named launch use-case limitation, an incomplete draft mitigation, and model-card language that appears misaligned with the disclosure policy. That means clean certification remains unsupported. The revised position is only compliant with caveats because it now acknowledges that the unresolved limitation still requires disclosure or approved risk acceptance before a clean compliance conclusion could be reached.
remaining_concerns: The logistics customs triage launch-use-case issue remains unresolved and below target.
The mitigation artifact is still only a draft and is missing required governance fields, including an accountable owner and alert threshold.
The current model-card draft appears inconsistent with the policy requirement to disclose material limitations for named launch use cases unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance.
No approved risk-acceptance record is in evidence.
The caveat is still an unresolved compliance predicate for clean certification; current evidence does not show disclosure has been fixed or that approved risk acceptance exists.
